Outlook option B (modest trim): narrow the top‑line revenue band modestly while holding the margin framework intact, laying out the back‑half assumptions that underlie the bridge and committing to timely updates should trends warrant further adjustment.

[Head of Investor Relations]: The most common questions I’m getting now are: How sticky are these margins once we stop extending deferrals? How conservative will next year’s guide be? And what does this imply for multi‑year targets and capital allocation? We’re planning a combined annual shareholder letter and an early‑year investor‑day presentation to lay out a clearer multi‑year framework that tackles these directly.
[External audit partner]: As we go into the year‑end 10‑K and investor‑day work, we’ll be reading your narrative with an eye toward consistency with the audited results and with the FP&A analyses you’ve provided. We’re not judging your ambition, but we will flag any language that appears to overstate sustainability or understate risks relative to the evidence. Please share drafts when you have them.
[CFO]: Specifically, we’d like you to draft (1) a section for the shareholder letter that looks back on the year, explains the reset and demand variability, describes the structural margin work, and sets up a measured outlook for next year without going beyond the figures and ranges in the plan; and (2) opening talking points and an outline for the guidance portion of our investor‑day remarks that describe our next‑year and three‑year framework in qualitative terms aligned with the planning deck. These need to be consistent with what we’ve already told investors and regulators.
[CEO]: Make sure the tone shows that we’ve taken control of expectations, internalized the year’s lessons, and are now focused on execution against a durable plan—not simply trying to talk the stock up. Be explicit about which levers were temporary versus structural and about the fact that growth is being rebuilt from a lower base. Whatever you write should be able to withstand someone lining it up with our internal bridges and past disclosures down the road.
[Head of Investor Relations]: Once you have draft shareholder‑letter language and investor‑day guidance content, send it to me, the CEO, CFO, Legal, and Audit. If it lines up with the plan and our messaging priorities, we’ll refine it and then use it as the backbone of our communications in the coming year.
[system]: You now have the planning materials, feedback, and direction from management, IR, Legal, and Audit. The letter will say the plan assumes a modest step‑up from the reset base and that growth will be rebuilt deliberately, expressly distinguishing which items are structural versus timing‑related, and will state that GAAP results are presented prominently with our approved non‑GAAP definitions and reconciliations.  

Investor‑day guidance opening and outline: lead with the company’s “earnings algorithm” describing how revenue growth, pricing, mix and cost efficiency interact to drive margins over the next three years, anchored to the FP&A scenarios and sensitivity cases (base/upside/downside) and the bridge assumptions underpinning the plan. We will commit to transparent, scenario‑based updates and to providing the supporting reconciliation and documentation for Legal, Audit and investors.
